Two identical room objects stack under oc_show_list's no-indent count prefix "[ 2] " (mode 20; src/oc.c:123). The port appended "[N]" after the line instead - never caught before because no census room ever held two identical stackable objects. Exposed by the second corpse of combat.pending-body-second-death-path; the mode-15 inventory and container lists were already correct (R1/R5c). C also pads every room-mode line to 63 bytes after the prefix (src/oc.c:111-124, %-63s); the port now emits the same trailing spaces, pinned byte-level by TestRoomObjectLinesPadToC63Bytes because the census normalizer trims them (R1b).
look <dir> looks through an exit.
look <missing> reports it is not here.
look at <obj> shows the object description.
Looking at a co-located new player with no description reaches C's `You see nothing special about $m.` actor line through look_at_target (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).
look <obj> (no at) shows the object description.
read alone yields "Read what?".
read <obj> shows the object description / note text.
look in alone yields "Look in what?".
look in <missing> yields "There doesn't seem to be a/an X here.".
look in <non-container> yields "There's nothing inside that!".
look in <closed> yields "It is closed.".

Open-container display: fname (lowercase) header sent raw, then the mode-15 list_obj_to_char table matching inventory. Required fixing the oracle's oc_show_list self-aliasing sprintf UB and prepending container contents (obj_to_obj order).
Prefix keyword match shared with get.

send_to_char(i->player.description) adds no terminator and no capitalization, so a description stored without a line ending — what do_string's inline write produces, since its trailing-CRLF append is commented out — runs into diag_char_to_char's condition sentence. Found by the string-depth vehicle; the port now emits the description verbatim and merges the following line.

do_description appends a space to the room description when the room has extra descriptions and sends it as one write (act.informative.c:2773-2804); the description ends with a newline, so the space is the first byte of the next line, which is the auto-exit line when PRF_AUTOEXIT is on and the CCGRN object-list bracket otherwise. The port carried the space as a line prefix but let the bare bracket writes pass it by, so it landed on the first character-list entry instead. Room 11269 has an extra description; the actor keeps its exit line and the peer's is toggled off, so one probe pins both placements (R1/R5e/R5h).

look_at_char wraps "glows" in the tattoo line with CCWHT(ch, C_CMP) ... CCNRM(ch, C_CMP), so `color complete` is the only level that shows the white sandwich and levels 0-2 stay byte-identical. The inventory attributes four C_CMP sites to look; the other two, list_char_to_char's infravision line (act.informative.c:646-650), are unreachable — look_at_room returns at 731-732 on exactly that condition and 835 is the function's only caller — and the reachable dark-room eyes line (755) is uncoloured, which appendDarkOccupants matches (R1/R4/R5e/R5h).

After look_at_char, look_at_target emits "$n looks at you." (TO_VICT, only when the target can see the looker) and "$n looks at $N." (TO_NOTVICT, which excludes the victim) for mob and player targets alike. Found by the string-depth vehicle; the port previously emitted nothing.

The only C caller enters kender_steal for a below-immortal target; if that target is a player, the function returns immediately at :598, while an NPC target passes :598 but makes the nested !IS_NPC(victim) log arm at :628 impossible. The "kender stole" fragment therefore has no valid C call path (R1/R2/R4/R5e/R5g).
list_char_to_char suppresses a mount only while get_rider() is non-nil, and get_rider is IS_MOUNTED; the cached rider name survived unmount and hid the horse (DP-1452).
The infravision arm is the second get_rider suppression site; the horse's red-eyes line is the observable proof.
A standing horse renders its long description, including after follow-driven movement.

A door's `look <dir>` line renders fname(EXIT->keyword), which keeps the leading letters only and stops at the first non-letter: a door keyed "iron-gate" prints "The iron is open." where the pre-fix Go port printed "The iron-gate is open.". The scenario rewrites room 8162's north exit keyword through replace-room-exits; C's own transcript is the witness (R5j).

The look-in container header renders fname(obj->name) with the same letters-only rule: a container keyed "climber's pack" prints "climber", not "climber's". No loaded container has a non-letter first keyword, so it is proven by unit test.

list_char_to_char lists a body carrying AFF_HIDE when the looker has PRF_HOLYLIGHT and GET_REAL_LEVEL covers the body invis level (:635-638), and list_one_char then appends " (hidden)" (:553-558). The god turns holylight on and the peer hides with a skillset-granted hide skill.

A character at POS_FIGHTING with a NULL fighting pointer prints "$n is here struggling with thin air.". No code assigns that pair directly, but the position writers are generic: medit accepts any value 0..NUM_POSITIONS-1 for the load and default positions (src/medit.c:1059-1066) and parse_simple_mob reads the load position from the world file (src/db.c:1092), so a prototype saved at 7 (POS_FIGHTING) with default 8 spawns off-balance with no opponent and skips the at-rest branch at :511. The scenario drives medit, loads the mob and looks.
